Keys: 1 separate · 2 joining · 3 joined · 4 shade · J / S cycle join and shade options · M steps Checks through its sizes · Esc cancels a drag. On the cloth hinge, drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to bend it, or focus it and press ↑ ↓. On the safety pin, drag GitDiscuss's nameplate round the pin (detents every 15°), and tap the pin to unpin it. On the button joint, drag GitDiscuss's nameplate round the button (it holds any angle), and tap the button to snip the shank. On the godet fan, drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to open or close the fan (detents every 15°), and tap the fan to unstrap it. On the sock heel, drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to knit or unravel the heel (each raspberry wedge is 15°), and tap the sock to frog it. On the cheese wedge, drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to pop slices in or squeeze them out (each slice is 15°), and tap the cheese to pull it apart. On the buckled strap, drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to slide the strap to another eyelet (each eyelet is 15°), and tap the strap or the buckle to unbuckle it. On the log rocker, drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to roll it up or down the log (each tick on its plank is 15°), and tap the log to lift it off. On the felt balloon, tap the balloon to fire the burner (GitDiscuss rises 15°) or the red tassel to vent it (it sinks 15°), or focus either and press Enter, ↑ or ↓; drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to tip it by hand, and tap the knuckles to release. On the bottlescrew, swipe across the cotton reel to turn it (down lets the stay out and GitDiscuss tips down, up screws it in and it tips up; it holds at any angle), or focus the reel and press ↑ ↓ to wind to the next 10° mark; drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to tip it by hand and the reel turns to match, and tap the button to release. On the lacing card, tug the bow out to draw the lace in (the wedge closes toward level) or push it back to give slack (it opens), or focus the bow and press ↑ ↓ for the next 15° mark; drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to open it by hand, and tap the gusset to unlace it. On the button tab, tug the tab to unbutton it. On the ribbon bow, pull a tail of the bow to untie it. On the appliqué patch, tap the patch and a seam ripper unpicks it. On the mitten hands, tug the handshake to make them let go. On the bunting, tug the garland to unhook it. On the bees, tap the festoons to send the bees off. On the padlock, tap the padlock to unlock it. On the fishing game, tap the line or the fish to let it go. On the pound-a-peg, tap the flaps to knock the pegs out. On the peg rail, tap the rail to lift GitDiscuss off the pegs. On the wet felt, tap the band and a carder combs it back into roving. On the woolly static, tap the balloon to discharge it, or tug it away to break the pull. Mitten friends adds stitched faces: pause a cushion with Ⅱ and it falls asleep. On the drawstring shade, pull a toggle down to open it. On the pleats shade, the piping on each fold is a status colour: amber running, blue idle or waiting, red needs you, green passed. On the woven label shade, the label's two border stripes are the status colour in the same scheme. On the toy piano shade, the note stickers on the keys are the status colours in the same scheme. On the turning blocks shade, tap the blocks (or focus them and press Enter, ↓ or ↑) to turn them to the next screen. On the washing line shade, the name and value are on the laundry name tape. On the frogged shade, the ball band's dye swatch is the status colour. On the sewing box shade, the middle spool's thread is the status colour, and the box keeps each widget's foot where it stood, so the strip ends up lower on the stage. On the plughole shade, the plug hanging over the bath's end is the status colour, and the bath keeps each widget's foot where it stood. On the hair bobble, tap the bobble to unhook it and slide it back off the plaits. On the wind-up hen, turn the key (or drag GitDiscuss's nameplate) clockwise to wind GitDiscuss down a click at a time; it won't turn back while the hen's beak is in the teeth, so tap the hen (or press ↑ on the key) to let the spring turn it back up a tooth, and tap the button hub to release. On the draught dog, tap the dog to pull its stitches out and let the stuffing puff out. On the bean bag, tap the bag to heave it out of the gap and send it hopping home. On the buttonhole crank, drag the navy shank button round to turn the crank (keep turning and GitDiscuss rocks back), tap it (or press Enter) for one steady turn that shows the quick return, or focus it and press ↑ ↓ for the next 15° mark; drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to tip it by hand and the crank keeps up, and tap the pivot button to release. On the daisy cam, drag the daisy round (let go and the bead drops into the nearest seat between two petals), tap it (or press Enter) to turn it one petal on, or focus it and press ↑ ↓ to turn to the nearest seat 15° higher or lower; drag GitDiscuss's nameplate to tip it by hand and the daisy keeps up, and tap the pivot button to release. On the iron shade, the iron's pilot light and the little felt iron on the name tape are the status colour, and the strip keeps each widget's foot where it stood. Checks has no joining edges, as in the capsule study. Chrome moves at 12 frames a second and the felt fibres shift each frame, like stop-motion; displays and dragging stay smooth. Nothing moves at rest.
